- Frameworks (caret, tidymodels, mlr3) offer varying levels of spatial data
integration, with CAST, blockCV, and waywiser enhancing their spatial capabilities
- Advanced methods like RandomForestsGLS, spatialRF, and meteo incorporate
spatial dependencies into the models but require careful data preparation
and understanding of their unique functionalities
- Spatial validation tools (e.g., blockCV, sperrorest) help mitigate biases when
selecting features and tuning hyperparameters, as well as assessing model
- Trade-offs exist between flexibility and complexity — some tools require
extensive workflows, while others are model-specific. There is also a noticeable
overlap in functionalities across different packages, while still offering unique
features that cater to specific spatial machine learning needs
- spatial methods depend on additional packages
